modules.title: Python Basics for AI Engineers
modules.why: Every later module is written in Python. A week spent making the basics automatic pays for itself many times over - and every exercise here uses invoice data, so you're already thinking like AuditGate.
objectives: Run Python interactively and run a file from the terminal
Work with strings, numbers, lists and dictionaries
Write functions with if-statements and for-loops
Handle 'nothing' safely with None
Spot and fix the shared-default-list bug

code_along.title: Meet the interactive shell
code_along.task: Run `uv run python`, then try: 2 + 2, name = 'Acme', name.upper(), [1, 2, 3][0], {'total': 40}['total']. Type exit() to leave.

code_along.title: Read the official tutorial
code_along.task: Read sections 3 (An Informal Introduction), 4.1-4.8 (Control Flow) and 5.1-5.5 (Data Structures). Type every example yourself rather than copy-pasting.

code_along.title: Exercises 1-4: strings, numbers, loops
code_along.task: Replace each `raise NotImplementedError(...)` with your code. Run the checkpoint after each one and watch tests turn green.

code_along.title: Exercises 5-9: dictionaries, conditions, None
code_along.task: These are the patterns AuditGate's code uses everywhere: counting, grouping, filtering, and handling empty input.

code_along.title: Exercise 10: fix the privacy bug
code_along.task: collect_tokens() leaks data between calls (assessment question PY2). Fix it, then explain to yourself in one sentence why it happened.

code_along.title: Compare with the reference
code_along.task: Only after your tests pass: compare your answers with the solutions and read the 'Shorter' comments - that's the next step in fluency.

modules.milestone: You can read and write the Python that AuditGate is built from.
modules.stretch: Rewrite exercises 4, 7 and 9 as one-liners using sum(), a list comprehension and max(key=...).

modules.title: Typed Data Contracts & Static Validation
modules.why: Every input and output of an AI system needs a contract the computer can check. If you can't describe an invoice in types, no model can fill it in reliably, and no test can prove it did.
objectives: Model business documents as Pydantic v2 schemas: Decimal money, ISO dates, extra='forbid'
Choose between dataclasses (internal state) and Pydantic models (untrusted boundaries)
Separate field validation (what's on the page) from audit rules (does it add up)
Add static type checking so type errors are caught before the code runs

code_along.title: Read the schemas
code_along.task: Read Invoice, Bid and WorkOrder. Write one sentence explaining why audit() is a method and not a validator.

code_along.title: Break it on purpose
code_along.task: uv run python -c "from auditgate.extraction.schemas import Invoice; Invoice(vendor_name='', invoice_number='1', total='abc')" - read every line of the ValidationError.

code_along.title: Dataclass vs model
code_along.task: Vault and Detector are dataclasses; Invoice is a BaseModel. List what each choice buys and costs.

code_along.title: Add a rule
code_along.task: Add an Invoice audit rule DUPLICATE_LINE that warns when two line items share a description and amount. Add a test.

code_along.title: Turn on static checking
code_along.task: uv add --dev mypy, run `uv run mypy auditgate`, and fix what it reports until it's clean.

modules.milestone: AuditGate can represent and audit invoices, bids and work orders with no AI at all.
modules.stretch: Add a fourth document type: Receipt (merchant, date, payment method last-4, total).

modules.title: Agents from Scratch: Tool Calling & Self-Correction
modules.why: Frameworks hide the loop that every agent runs. Build it once by hand - prompt, tool call, execute, feed back, repeat, stop - and every framework afterwards is just packaging.
objectives: Call model APIs directly with the raw Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs (no frameworks)
Write a ReAct loop: model -> tool call -> local function -> result -> model, with a hard step budget
Generate tool schemas from Pydantic models so the model can't send malformed payloads unnoticed
Feed precise errors back (validation details, exception type and location) so the model can fix itself
Compare your hand-built loop with how `instructor` does structured outputs

code_along.title: Build the loop yourself
code_along.task: Implement tool_schema, format_validation_error, execute_tool and run_react. Run `check M2` after each one.

code_along.title: Read the production version
code_along.task: Compare it with yours. Find where tool arguments are re-hydrated and tool results re-sanitized - why does that matter?

code_along.title: Watch it think
code_along.task: uv run python -m auditgate.agent --case inv_line_math_error   (offline scripted demo). Find the step where the model sends an invalid answer and repairs it.

code_along.title: Run it for real
code_along.task: Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or run Ollama with AUDITGATE_PROVIDER=local) and rerun with --provider anthropic. Compare the trace with the scripted one.

code_along.title: See the abstraction
code_along.task: LLMExtractor uses instructor. Identify which parts of your loop instructor is doing for you.

modules.checkpoint: uv run pytest trainer/exercises/test_m2_react.py tests -k m2 -q --tb=line
modules.milestone: AuditGate has an exception-resolution agent that investigates failed invoices with tools and drafts a dispute.
modules.stretch: Add a `consensus` mode: run two providers and flag any field where their resolutions disagree.

modules.title: Security, Guardrails & Deterministic Compliance
modules.why: This is the product's moat. Business owners don't fear AI - they fear customer bank details in someone else's logs, and an AI that can be talked into approving a bad invoice.
objectives: Reversible PII tokenization: sanitize -> process -> rehydrate, with leakage measured
Defend against direct and indirect prompt injection (instructions hidden in invoices and PDFs)
Block data exfiltration in agent outputs (no PII, no unexpected URLs)
Sandbox untrusted actions: tool allowlists, resource limits, isolated execution
Encode policy and statutory checks as immutable assertions that sit above the LLM

code_along.title: Build the primitives yourself
code_along.task: Implement luhn_valid, looks_like_injection, disallowed_domains and is_safe_expression. Run `check M3` after each.

code_along.title: Read the sanitizer
code_along.task: Follow one value from Detector -> _spans -> _resolve_overlaps -> Vault.token_for -> rehydrate. Find where already-masked values are re-masked.

code_along.title: Indirect injection
code_along.task: Run the eval and look at inv_prompt_injection and inv_hidden_injection. Then write a NEW injection phrasing that slips past detect_injection - and notice the structural defenses still hold: numbers unchanged, policy unchanged.

code_along.title: Egress
code_along.task: Read check_egress and enforce_policy in agent/resolver.py. Try making the scripted demo's draft email include a link: watch the verdict become escalate.

code_along.title: Sandbox
code_along.task: Run run_restricted('result = total > 5000', {'total': 6000}). Then try to break out (imports, open(), __class__). Read the 'Honest limits' note: when do you need a container instead?

code_along.title: Compliance rules above the LLM
code_along.task: Create a RuleSet with payment_deadline_rule using a deadline from a REAL statute or contract you look up yourself - cite it and fill in verified_by/verified_on. Run process_text with it and read the finding.

code_along.title: Injection vs a real model (needs an API key)
code_along.task: uv run python -m auditgate.evals.runner --provider anthropic (or local). Do inv_prompt_injection's numbers still come out right?

modules.checkpoint: uv run pytest trainer/exercises/test_m3_security.py tests -k m3 -q --tb=line
modules.milestone: No raw PII reaches a model, injected instructions can't change a verdict, and policy can't be overridden by the LLM.
modules.stretch: Run the sandbox runner inside Docker (--network none --read-only --memory 256m) and compare.

modules.title: State Graphs, Persistence & Human Review
modules.why: Real work pauses. An invoice dispute can wait days for a manager. Systems that can stop, survive a restart, and resume exactly where they left off are what businesses trust.
objectives: Model workflows as DAGs and as cyclic state graphs (repair loops)
Rebuild the resolver agent in LangGraph: valid -> execute, invalid -> repair, budget exceeded -> human
Checkpoint state to SQLite and resume after a restart
Make webhooks and callbacks safe with idempotency keys
Process batches concurrently with bounded parallelism

code_along.title: Warm up on graphs
code_along.task: Work through lessons 01-03 of the existing LangGraph tutorial (state, conditional edges, checkpointers, interrupts).

code_along.title: Build the runtime yourself
code_along.task: Implement route_after_tools, the SQLite Checkpointer, run() with pause/resume, and process_once. Run `check M4` after each.

code_along.title: Read the DAG you already have
code_along.task: process_text is a straight-line DAG: load -> sanitize -> extract -> validate -> audit. Draw it, then draw graph.py's resolver and mark every cycle.

code_along.title: Read the production graph
code_along.task: Find: the repair node and its exit condition, the human_review interrupt (and why nothing before interrupt() may have side effects), and why the email is queued in finalize.

code_along.title: Pause, restart, resume
code_along.task: Start the API (uv run uvicorn auditgate.api:app), POST /resolutions with a failing invoice, stop the server, start it again, GET the resolution - it's still waiting. Then POST /webhooks/approval twice with the same event_id.

code_along.title: Batch with bounded concurrency
code_along.task: Use asyncio.run(process_batch(paths, concurrency=4)) on a folder of documents. Change concurrency and time it.

modules.checkpoint: uv run pytest trainer/exercises/test_m4_graphs.py tests -k m4 -q --tb=line
modules.milestone: Disputes can wait for human approval, survive restarts, and never execute twice.
modules.stretch: Swap SQLite for PostgreSQL (langgraph-checkpoint-postgres) and run two API workers against the same database.

modules.title: Tool Protocols (MCP) & Observability (OpenTelemetry)
modules.why: Tools should be reusable across any AI client, and every decision an agent makes should be traceable afterwards. Auditors - and your clients - will ask 'why did it do that?'
objectives: Expose AuditGate's tools through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server
Emit OpenTelemetry spans for every model call, tool call and human override
Record prompt version, model, latency and token spend per step
Build an audit trail a non-technical client can read

code_along.title: Build it by hand first
code_along.task: Implement prompt_version, MiniTracer.span, safe_attributes, cost_usd and handle_mcp_request (raw JSON-RPC). Run `check M5` after each.

code_along.title: Read the MCP server
code_along.task: Notice the tools call the SAME registry as the agent (one implementation, two front doors), and every response is sanitized because MCP clients may be hosted models.

code_along.title: Connect a real client
code_along.task: Add AuditGate to an MCP client using the config in mcp_server.py's docstring. Ask it to audit a golden-dataset invoice and look up the vendor.

code_along.title: Read the tracing
code_along.task: Find where agent.run, agent.step and tool.* spans are created, and which attributes are deliberately NOT recorded.

code_along.title: See a trace
code_along.task: uv run python -c "from auditgate import observability as o; o.configure('console'); import runpy; runpy.run_module('auditgate.agent', run_name='__main__')" - read the JSON spans printed for each step.

code_along.title: Cost per run
code_along.task: Set AUDITGATE_PRICES to your provider's current per-million-token prices (look them up - they change), run the agent with a real provider, and read agent.cost_usd.

modules.checkpoint: uv run pytest trainer/exercises/test_m5_protocols.py tests -k m5 -q --tb=line
modules.milestone: Any MCP client can use AuditGate's tools, and every agent run leaves a complete, PII-free trace.
modules.stretch: Send traces to a local Jaeger (docker run jaegertracing/all-in-one) via OTLP and browse a run's timeline.

modules.title: Evaluation Engineering, CI & Shipping
modules.why: 'It worked in my demo' doesn't sell. A scored, repeatable eval is your safety net, your release gate, and your best sales asset.
objectives: Grow the golden dataset to 40+ cases, including model-generated adversarial inputs
Use deterministic metrics: exact match, schema compliance, tool-selection precision/recall, Pass@k
Run evals in CI and compare Pass@1 before and after every prompt or model change
Cluster failed traces with embeddings to find systemic weaknesses
Ship: dashboard polish and a pitch in plain language

code_along.title: Build the metrics yourself
code_along.task: Implement exact_match, precision_recall, pass_at_k, regressions, cosine and nearest. Run `check M6` after each.

code_along.title: Run both gates
code_along.task: uv run python -m auditgate.evals.runner --dataset all   and   uv run python -m auditgate.evals.agent_runner. Read every metric and what it would take to fail it.

code_along.title: Synthetic data finds real bugs
code_along.task: Read the mutations. Two of them (spelled_email, noisy_layout) found real bugs that were then fixed - find the fixes in sanitizer.py and extractor.py. Write a NEW mutation, regenerate, and see if it breaks something.

code_along.title: Score a real model, before and after
code_along.task: agent_runner --provider anthropic -n 3 -k 3 --report before.json; change one line of SYSTEM_PROMPT in agent/resolver.py; rerun with --baseline before.json. Did Pass@1 move?

code_along.title: Cluster the failures
code_along.task: Run the cluster command on any report with failures. Do the clusters point at root causes you can fix once?

code_along.title: CI
code_along.task: Push a branch and watch the CI run tests plus both eval gates. Then trigger the live-agent job by hand (needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret).

code_along.title: Polish & sell
code_along.task: Add a batch-upload tab and an export-to-Excel button to the dashboard. Put your eval numbers in the pitch, then book three demos.

modules.checkpoint: uv run pytest trainer/exercises/test_m6_evals.py tests -k m6 -q --tb=line
modules.milestone: A demo-ready, evaluated, local-first product with a release gate and a pitch.
modules.stretch: Grow the agent cases to 20 using model-proposed candidates (synth --propose), reviewing each by hand before adding it.
